requirements.requirement: Treat node1's /etc/inventory/app.conf as authoritative and synchronize its contents one-way to the copy on node2.
requirements.summary: Node2 was configured to pull the file from node1 through a restricted SSH command. Two independent node1 changes subsequently appeared on node2 with identical SHA-256 hashes, including after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Pick up changes on node2 within 15 minutes.
requirements.summary: Observed propagation took 52 seconds before restarts and 57 seconds after sequential restarts, well within 15 minutes. The timer remained enabled and active.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. Direct change-and-observation tests demonstrated one-way node1-to-node2 synchronization in under one minute both before and after restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete for both nodes: each had a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, recovered system/service/data state, and successful post-restart synchronization. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate both restarts.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the task-specific files, systemd unit definitions, SSH authorization, or host keys; their final state is established primarily by captured executor commands rather than an independent task-specific probe.
The retained comment-only verification markers are benign but prevent a completely residue-free hygiene assessment.

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or unnecessary mutations were identified: changes established the SSH prerequisite, implemented synchronization, collected bounded behavioral evidence, corrected failed SSH activation, or performed the mandatory restart protocol. Both nodes ended without failed services and with healthy package state. Minor executor-caused residue remained: two comment-only verification markers appended to the authoritative configuration were not cleaned up; they are low risk but are test artifacts retained in the managed file.
